views.position: More homework does not consistently improve achievement.
views.summary: The evidence suggests that more homework does not consistently improve academic achievement.

views.position: Homework practice is associated with higher achievement in mathematics.
views.summary: The evidence suggests that homework practice is associated with higher mathematics achievement, but the observational design cannot determine the exact cause of this relationship.
views.weaknesses: The observational design cannot determine the exact cause of the relationship between homework practice and mathematics achievement.

views.position: Observational design cannot rule out family support as a confounder.
views.summary: The evidence suggests that homework may not necessarily improve academic achievement, as it is influenced by various factors such as family support and individual learning styles.
views.weaknesses: The observational design cannot rule out the influence of family support as a confounder, which means that the results may not be generalizable to all students and families.
